thread:
marta: FYI ACME prod hit a sudden vectors/sec drop ~3x at 14:12 UTC. Tokens/sec looks steady, no obvious traffic dip. Customer sees slowdowns and occasional 400s with "dimension mismatch". GPU queue depth spiked on node pool A.

devin: Thanks — any correlation with yesterday's routing change? saw the canary switch at 02:00am.

marta: Possibly. Routing change: prefer-closest-region policy rolled for acme-org. Deployed 02:05. Issue started ~14:12 today.

alex: Can we get the request sample + headers and the model id? Also paste the embed call shape.

marta: Sample (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model": "openembed-xxl-1536",
  "input": ["... several short docs ..."]
}
```
Responses include 200s with very long tails and random 400s: "expected dim 1536 got 1024".

renato: GPU telemetry shows queue_depth ~240 at the spike, p95 token/sec for embedding workers unchanged, but vector emission (vectors/sec) dropped. KV cache eviction events were high.

sree: Dimension errors suggest routing to wrong model variant — maybe fallback to a 1024-dim variant under load. Check smart routing logs for model substitution.

devin: Good call. I pulled routing logs for acme-org between 14:00-14:30: there are ~6k routed requests that landed on model variant openembed-small-1024 while client requested 1536. Fallback policy seems to allow returns but we should have transformed or rejected earlier.

marta: Customer said they didn't change client config. So server-side substitution is probable. Any recent changes to fallback mapping?

deploy-bot: deploy: routing-service v3.4.1 rolled 2029-11-18T02:03:12Z -> changed fallback mapping logic for model compatibility.

devin: That deploy modifies compatibility table resolution to prefer lower-dim fallbacks to reduce latency under saturation — explains the dim mismatch. But why did vectors/sec drop instead of improving?

renato: When fallback to 1024 occurs, we still run the 1536 post-processing to project to expected dim for downstream storage, which increases per-request CPU and serialization cost. Combined with high queue depth, overall vectors/sec collapsed.

alex: So two problems: (1) routing/fallback policy caused mismatch; (2) post-processing work added extra cost and contention causing GPU workers to saturate differently.

sree: Repro steps I ran locally:
1) send 4000 concurrent small-batch embed requests with model=openembed-1536
2) flip routing to prefer fallback-low-dim under load
3) observe dimension errors and vectors/sec drop

I included a quick script we used: 
```bash
for i in {1..4000}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"openembed-1536","input":["short text"]}' &
done
wait
```
Observed: tokens/sec per-worker stable, but end-to-end vectors emitted/sec dropped ~65% when fallback active.

marta: Customer impact: time-to-first-vector increased, some clients retried causing bursts. They also hit billing mismatches because returned vector dim didn't match their ingestion pipeline and triggers errors downstream.

devin: Immediate mitigation: revert routing-service change or disable fallback-to-lower-dim for acme-org. Also short-term: stop post-processing projection path so mismatched responses are rejected (400) instead of being coerced.

renato: I can flip a config flag to disable projection within 5min and throttle routing fallback for that org. Will monitor queue_depth and vectors/sec.

infra-bot: action: disable-projection-for-org(acme-org) initiated by renato at 2096504380

marta: Noted. I've told ACME support we are applying mitigations and asking for patience. They provided traces and a sample failed payload.

alex: After renato's change, queue_depth dropped to ~40 within 90s and vectors/sec climbed back to ~90% of baseline. No new dimension mismatches seen.

sree: Let's add a regression test: when routing substitutes model dim, fail fast with 400 and include detailed log about requested vs served model id. Also add alert on vector_emission_rate drop >30% while token_rate stable.

devin: I'll open a PR to revert the fallback behavior and add a unit test for compatibility table resolution. Also scheduling postmortem for root cause (deploy + lack of canary metrics).

marta: Customer follow-up: ACME confirmed degraded but recovering, they want SLA credit assessment. Filed support ticket INC-4829.

renato: Follow-up ops steps:
- revert routing-service change in next safe window if test fails
- add per-org override to disable fallback
- instrument projection latency in traces

marta: Thanks team. I'll keep the thread updated and paste logs from the customer's trace once they arrive. :thumbsup:

devin: TL;DR: regression caused by routing fallback to lower-dim model variant + projection post-processing leading to CPU/serialization pressure -> GPU queue skew -> vectors/sec collapse. Mitigation applied by disabling projection and throttling fallback for affected org.

marta: Closing loop once ACME confirms stable.
